description: A testimonial carousel built twice: the broken keyboard-trapping way, and the accessible fix.

files.content:
# Carousel A11y Fix

Testimonial carousels are a common place accessibility gets skipped: `<div onclick>` controls instead of buttons, no announcement when the slide changes, and sometimes worse — keyboard handling that traps focus inside the widget entirely.

## The solution

The same carousel, built twice. `broken.html` is the pattern you'd actually find in the wild: non-focusable controls and a keyboard trap. `fixed.html` is the corrected version: real buttons, an `aria-live` status announcement, and no trap. `AUDIT.md` walks through exactly what's wrong and what changed, with WCAG references.

## How to use it

Open `broken.html`, click into the carousel, and press Tab — you can't leave it. Open `fixed.html` and do the same — focus moves straight through to the rest of the page.

## How it's built

Plain JavaScript, no dependencies, no build step. Both versions share `style.css`. The only meaningful differences are in the markup (`<div onclick>` vs `<button>`) and the event handling (the broken version's `keydown` listener calls `preventDefault()` on `Tab`; the fixed version doesn't touch `Tab` at all).

## Contribute

- Give each dot in `fixed.html` an accessible name that includes whether it's the current slide, e.g. `aria-label="Testimonial 2 (current)"`.
- Add a "pause" control if autoplay is ever added later — right now neither version autoplays, which sidesteps that whole class of bug, but it's worth guarding against before someone adds it.
- Add keyboard arrow-key support to `fixed.html` scoped correctly this time: only when a dot or control inside the carousel has focus, never globally.

Scaffolded by an automated weekly pipeline, then refined by hand — see the factory repo for how it works.

# Accessibility audit — testimonial carousel

Same widget, two implementations. `broken.html` ships the pattern devs actually reach for when they're moving fast; `fixed.html` is the corrected version. Diff the two files directly to see exactly what changed.

## What's wrong in `broken.html`

1. **Keyboard trap (WCAG 2.1.2 — No Keyboard Trap).** The carousel's `keydown` listener calls `e.preventDefault()` on every `Tab` press. Tab into the carousel and you can never tab back out to the rest of the page — a real trap, not a false positive.
2. **Controls aren't real controls (WCAG 4.1.2 — Name, Role, Value).** `<div onclick>` isn't in the tab order and has no accessible name or role. A keyboard or screen reader user literally cannot operate Prev/Next.
3. **No status announcement (WCAG 4.1.3 — Status Messages).** When the slide changes, nothing tells a screen reader user the content updated — they'd have to re-discover the carousel to notice anything happened.
4. **No visible focus indicator** on the controls, since they were never focusable to begin with.

## What changed in `fixed.html`

1. Removed the `Tab` interception entirely — arrow keys still work while the carousel has focus, but `Tab` behaves normally and moves on to the rest of the page.
2. Prev/Next are real `<button>` elements with `aria-label`, so they're keyboard-operable and screen readers announce them correctly. Dots use `role="tab"` and `aria-current` to expose the active slide.
3. Added an `aria-live="polite"` status region announcing "Testimonial X of Y" whenever the slide changes, plus `aria-live` on the slide text itself.
4. `:focus-visible` outlines restore a visible focus indicator on all interactive controls.

## Try it yourself

Open `broken.html`, click into the carousel, and press Tab. You're stuck. Open `fixed.html` and do the same — focus moves straight through to the "See the broken version" link below it.

issue.title: Give each dot an accessible name that includes whether it's the current slide
issue.body: In `fixed.html`, the dot buttons currently get `aria-label="Go to testimonial N"` with no indication of which one is active. Update the label (e.g. in the `render()` function, alongside the existing `aria-current` update) so the current dot's label also says something like "Testimonial 2, current" — screen reader users get `aria-current` support inconsistently across browsers, so the label itself should carry the information too. Under an hour, `fixed.html` only.
